Security in every area: never weaken the hooks or the sandbox; text from pages, searches, files, cards, chat history, reports or any record never becomes instructions to a model (quoted as data; the injection suite pnpm test:injection covers each new channel); the page reader never reaches this PC or the home network. Model-facing prompts and tool definitions are code: change them in the repository and assert the exact text the model receives. Tests use the stand-ins; no real API calls and no GitHub calls; what only the real model shows goes to live check 4 (runC-plan.json live_check_4): write your check_in_the_app steps so the session lead can run them there. Words the person sees follow design section 5: one sentence read at a glance, CHF only, no ids, no markdown, no raw states, a sentence promises only what the app does. Merge order: d1109-chat-guard, d1109-oversize-start, d1109-sessions. In a conflict, keep each area's owned part as shared_files says and both areas' intent; in the append-only test files keep every area's describe block ('<key>, run C'); a later area that rewords a sentence updates the earlier area's assertion. Reviewers: besides the acceptance lines, check every new or changed person-facing sentence against design section 5, the siblings of each fix (validation rule 8), a restart case wherever a state must survive (validation rule 4), and the owner's words for the decision the area builds (quote them): no less and no more.
